env.prompt: Asana MCP app Client ID (developer console → your MCP app → OAuth)

entries.description: Tasks, projects, and goals from your Asana workspace.
entries.name: asana
entries.post_install:
Asana V2 has no Dynamic Client Registration: you need your own Asana
MCP app. In the developer console (https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps)
create an app of type "MCP app", then:
  - OAuth → Redirect URL: http://localhost:27890/callback (exactly).
  - Manage distribution → allow the workspace(s) you will use.
Its Client ID / Client secret are the ASANA_CLIENT_ID / ASANA_CLIENT_SECRET
values prompted above. The secret is stored in the profile's .env; the
non-secret client id is inlined into config.yaml.

Then run `duckwork mcp login asana` (or click Authorize in the dashboard /
Desktop: the callback still arrives at http://localhost:27890/callback, so
the browser must run on the same machine as Duckwork), approve access, and
restart (or `/reload-mcp`) the Duckwork session or gateway that should
expose the Asana tools.

entries.description: Full Cloudflare API access via the official remote MCP.
entries.name: cloudflare
entries.post_install:
On first connection, Duckwork opens a browser to authorize with Cloudflare.
You pick the account and the permissions to grant — scope the token to
what you want the agent to touch. After auth, restart your Duckwork session
so the Cloudflare tools are loaded.

This entry exposes each Cloudflare API endpoint as an individual tool.
A curated exclude list ships in the manifest (enterprise-contract,
org-fleet, and read-only-analytics product families are disabled —
~1,400 tools), leaving ~1,900 tools for the products people actually
drive from an agent: DNS, Workers, R2, KV, D1, Queues, Pages, WAF,
rulesets, tunnels, Access, Stream, Images, AI, Vectorize. Duckwork's
tool_search defers them all, so your context is not flooded — the agent
discovers the right endpoint on demand with full schemas.

Run a Zero Trust org or want Radar/Magic/API-Shield surfaces back?
Delete their patterns from mcp_servers.cloudflare.tools.exclude in
~/.duckwork/config.yaml.

Headless / CI alternative: instead of OAuth, create a Cloudflare API token
at https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens and configure the server
with a bearer header in ~/.duckwork/config.yaml:

  mcp_servers:
    cloudflare:
      url: "https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp?codemode=false"
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}"

Prefer the provider-side Code Mode surface instead (2 search/execute
meta-tools, ~1k-token schema, sandboxed JS composition)? Drop the
`?codemode=false` from the url. Not recommended together with Duckwork
tool_search — you'd be stacking two tool-discovery layers.

Cloudflare also runs product-specific MCP servers (same OAuth flow, add
manually via `duckwork mcp add <name> --url <url>` if you want a narrower
surface): docs search (https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, no auth),
Workers observability (https://observability.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp),
Browser Rendering (https://browser.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp), Radar
(https://radar.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp), GraphQL analytics
(https://graphql.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp), audit logs
(https://auditlogs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp), and more — full list at the
source URL above.

Re-run the tool checklist any time with:
  duckwork mcp configure cloudflare

entries.description: Connect to your n8n instance's official MCP server with browser OAuth.
entries.name: n8n-official
entries.post_install:
In n8n Settings > Instance-level MCP, enable MCP access (owner or admin).
Open Connect and copy the full Server URL ending in /mcp-server/http.
Use that URL, not your editor URL. The Duckwork backend must be able to reach it.
On older n8n versions, the same endpoint is shown in the MCP settings page.

Run `duckwork mcp login n8n-official`, or use Authorize in the desktop app
or dashboard, and approve access in n8n. No n8n API key is required.
If your instance restricts OAuth callback URLs, allow the callback used by Duckwork.

n8n controls access through your account permissions and MCP settings.
Search can show previews of workflows you can view; enable Available in MCP
for workflows you want to inspect fully, execute, or modify. Tool availability
depends on your n8n version and permissions. Some tools change or run workflows.
Use `duckwork mcp configure n8n-official` to review the discovered tools.

Existing n8n bridge connections are unchanged. This is a separate connection,
not an automatic migration. Start a new session or use /reload-mcp after setup.

entries.description: Drive the Unreal Engine 5.8 editor over its local MCP server.
entries.name: unreal-engine
entries.post_install:
This entry connects to Epic's official Unreal MCP plugin, which runs INSIDE
the Unreal Editor. Before Duckwork can connect:

  1. Open your project in Unreal Editor 5.8+.
  2. Edit > Plugins, search "Unreal MCP", enable it, restart the editor
     (the Toolset Registry dependency enables automatically).
  3. Edit > Editor Preferences > General > Model Context Protocol, turn on
     "Auto Start Server" (or run `ModelContextProtocol.StartServer` in the
     editor console). It binds to http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp by default.

Start Duckwork AFTER the editor's server is running so the tools are probed.
If you changed the port or URL path in Editor Preferences, update the url in
mcp_servers.unreal-engine to match.

Status: Epic ships this as EXPERIMENTAL. The server runs Tool calls serially
on the engine game thread — avoid issuing overlapping calls.

Re-run the tool checklist any time with:
  duckwork mcp configure unreal-engine
